## 1. Instructions
- **Project:** `AGENTS.md`. V2 discovers the global file plus **every** `AGENTS.md` from the workspace directory up to the project root (or home, for workspaces inside home). They are combined; the nearest is not the only one.
- **Global:** `~/.config/opencode/AGENTS.md`. If it is missing, OpenCode falls back to `~/.claude/CLAUDE.md`.
- **`CLAUDE.md` fallback:** any directory without an `AGENTS.md` reads its `CLAUDE.md` instead. An `AGENTS.md` always wins over a sibling `CLAUDE.md`. Unlike V1, a root `AGENTS.md` no longer hides a nested `CLAUDE.md`.
- **More files:** list them in the `instructions` array in `opencode.json(c)` (paths, globs or HTTP(S) URLs). They load after `AGENTS.md` files.
- **Turning off Claude compatibility:**
  - `OPENCODE_DISABLE_PROJECT_CONFIG=1` skips project `AGENTS.md` discovery (keeps the global file);
  - `OPENCODE_DISABLE_CLAUDE_CODE_PROMPT=1` skips every `CLAUDE.md`;
  - `OPENCODE_DISABLE_CLAUDE_CODE=1` turns off all `.claude` support (prompt and skills).

## 2. Skills
- **Locations:** `.opencode/skills/`, `~/.config/opencode/skills/`, plus the compatibility folders `.claude/skills/`, `~/.claude/skills/`, `.agents/skills/` and `~/.agents/skills/`.
- **Forms:** a directory `<id>/SKILL.md` (recommended) or a flat `<id>.md` at the source root. A directory with `SKILL.md` is one skill.
- **IDs** come from the path, are case-sensitive, and are the key for loading and permissions. Prefer a lowercase-kebab ID that matches the folder name. Frontmatter `name` is only a display label (optional).
- **Frontmatter:**

  | Field | Notes |
  |---|---|
  | `name` | display label; defaults to the path-derived ID. Not required, need not match the folder. |
  | `description` | needed when the model should discover the skill. |
  | `metadata` | string→string map. `opencode/autoinvoke: "false"` hides the skill from the model's available list (it can still be loaded by ID). |
  | `disable-model-invocation` | `true` has the same effect as `opencode/autoinvoke: "false"`. `opencode/autoinvoke` wins if both are set. |
  | `license`, `compatibility` | accepted for portability, not interpreted. |

  The Agent Skills standard keys (`when_to_use`, `allowed-tools`, `context`, …) are ignored. V2 does not enforce kebab-case IDs, a name/folder match, or a description length, but portable skills should keep all three.
- **Invocation:**
  - The model calls the `skill` tool with the skill's ID (`skill({ id: "x" })`). Available skills are listed in that tool's description.
  - A user loads a skill by mentioning `@skill-id`.
  - To load another skill from inside a skill, say so explicitly: "call the skill tool with id `x`".
- **Access control:** `skill` action with the skill ID as the resource, `allow` / `ask` / `deny`. `deny` hides the skill from the model.
- **Duplicate IDs:** the later-registered source wins (override), so two copies with the same ID no longer error — but avoid duplicates unless you intend to override.
- **Bundled files:** refer to them by relative path from SKILL.md and state that they live in the skill's folder.

## 3. Agents
- **Locations:** `.opencode/agents/<name>.md` (project) or `~/.config/opencode/agents/<name>.md` (user). **The file name is the agent ID.** A nested path becomes part of the ID (`team/reviewer.md` → `team/reviewer`). Agents can also be defined under the `agents` key of `opencode.json(c)`.
- **Frontmatter:**

  | Field | Values / notes |
  |---|---|
  | `description` | required. Used for automatic delegation. |
  | `mode` | `primary` (main agent), `subagent` (invoked via the `subagent` tool or `@name`), `all`. **Defaults to `primary`** for a new custom agent. |
  | `model` | `provider/model-id`, optionally with a variant: `provider/model-id#variant`. Subagents inherit the invoking primary's model when omitted. |
  | `system` | system prompt; JSON config only — in a Markdown agent the body is the prompt. |
  | `permissions` | ordered `{action, resource, effect}` rules (section 4). |
  | `steps` | maximum model steps. |
  | `hidden` | hides the agent from listings and discovery (visibility, not security) |
  | `color` | six-digit hex, e.g. `"#ff6b6b"` |
  | `disabled` | `true` removes the agent |
  | `request` | per-agent header/body overlays (preserved but not yet sent to the model) |

  Deprecated V1 fields, auto-translated but ignored when a file uses V2 fields: `name`, `prompt` (→ `system`), `disable` (→ `disabled`), `permission` (→ `permissions`), `tools`, `temperature`, `top_p`, `maxSteps` (→ `steps`), `variant` (→ `#variant`). Do not mix V1 and V2 fields in one file.

- **Built-ins:** `build` (primary, all tools), `plan` (primary, edits restricted), `general` (subagent), `explore` (subagent, read-only). Hidden maintenance agents: `compaction`, `title`, `summary`. **V2 has no `scout` agent.**
- **Orchestration:** for an orchestrator, use a `mode: primary` agent or a skill, never a subagent. The `subagent` action controls which subagents an agent may launch.
- **CLI:** there is no `opencode agent` subcommand; edit the file or the `agents` config entry.

## 4. Permissions
V2 permissions are one ordered array of rules. The last matching rule wins, so put `"*"` first, exceptions after.

| Field | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `action` | Tool or permission action (wildcards allowed). |
| `resource` | Path, command, agent ID, skill ID, URL, query, etc. |
| `effect` | `allow`, `ask` or `deny`. |

Built-in actions and what each `resource` matches:

| Action | Resource |
|---|---|
| `read` | file path. `*.env` is `ask` by default. |
| `edit` | target path for edit, write and patch |
| `glob` | the glob pattern |
| `grep` | the regex |
| `shell` | scanner-produced command string |
| `subagent` | the subagent ID |
| `skill` | the skill ID |
| `question` | `*` |
| `webfetch` | the URL |
| `websearch` | the query |
| `experimental_image_generate` | `providerID/modelID` (plus `#variant`) |
| `external_directory` | external directory boundary. **Allowed by default in V2** (V1 asked) |
| `<server>_<tool>` | `*` for an MCP tool |
| `execute` | `*` (Code Mode) |

- **Patterns:** `*` and `?`. For `read`, `edit` and `external_directory`, a leading `~` or `$HOME` expands to home; shell resources stay raw command text.
- **Merging:** global rules load first, agent rules append after (they do not replace). A custom subagent uses its own permissions, not a subset of its parent's.
- **`bash` vs `shell` (re-tested 2026-11-22, v2.3.2):** `shell` is now the canonical action and is enforced; `bash` and `task` are deprecated V1 action names that OpenCode auto-translates to `shell` and `subagent`. On v2.3.2, `permissions: [{action: shell, resource: "*", effect: deny}]`, V1 `permission: {bash: {"*": deny}}` and V1 `permission: {shell: {"*": deny}}` each blocked a shell command (control agent without the rule ran it). Use `shell` and `subagent` in new config; V1 `permission`/`bash`/`task` still work but are deprecated. `--auto` does not override a `deny`.

Read-only reviewer example:
```yaml
permissions:
  - action: edit
    resource: "*"
    effect: deny
  - action: shell
    resource: "*"
    effect: deny
  - action: shell
    resource: "git diff --staged"
    effect: allow
  - action: shell
    resource: "git diff --staged -- *"
    effect: allow
  - action: webfetch
    resource: "*"
    effect: deny
  - action: websearch
    resource: "*"
    effect: deny
  - action: subagent
    resource: "*"
    effect: deny
```
Keep shell patterns exact. A trailing wildcard such as `"git diff*"` or `"git log *"` also admits `--output=<file>`, which writes a file. After `--`, git treats every argument as a path, so `"git diff --staged -- *"` is safe. A shell pattern ending in ` *` also matches the command with no arguments.

| Abstract capability | OpenCode permission action |
|---|---|
| read / search files | `read`, `glob`, `grep` |
| edit / create files | `edit` |
| run commands | `shell` |
| web | `webfetch`, `websearch` |
| delegate | `subagent` |
| load skills | `skill` |
| ask the user | `question` |

## 5. Models (DeepSeek)
- **Connecting:** `/connect` → DeepSeek, or set `DEEPSEEK_API_KEY`. `opencode models` lists the available IDs (no provider argument).
- **Model IDs** (`opencode models` on v2.3.2, models.dev and api-docs.deepseek.com, 2026-11-22):

  | ID | Model | Notes |
  |---|---|---|
  | `deepseek/deepseek-flash` | DeepSeek V4.1 Flash (1017) | 1M context, 384K max output, vision, cheapest. The default choice. |
  | `deepseek/deepseek-v4-pro` | DeepSeek V4 Pro (0813) | 1M context, no vision; for heavier text-only reasoning |

  The legacy `deepseek-v4-flash` and `deepseek-v4-flash-vision-exp` are retired: requests are served by V4.1 Flash and billed at the Flash price, and OpenCode hides them from the model list.

- **Tiers:**

  | Abstract tier | Value |
  |---|---|
  | same as caller | omit `model` (subagents inherit) |
  | fast / cheap | `deepseek/deepseek-flash` |
  | strongest | `deepseek/deepseek-v4-pro` |

- **DeepSeek specifics:**
  - Thinking is on by default; both models also support a non-thinking mode. `temperature` is ignored in thinking mode (applies only when thinking is off).
  - Context caching is automatic, so keep system prompts and skill text byte-stable. Cache-hit input is far cheaper than cache-miss.
  - Off-peak pricing is half price. Peak hours are 01:00–04:00 and 06:00–10:00 UTC, Mon–Fri, excluding Chinese public holidays.
  - Flash (per 1M tokens, off-peak): input $0.15 (cache hit $0.003), output $0.60. Pro: input $0.66 (cache hit $0.022), output $1.98. Peak is double.
  - DeepSeek models follow terse instructions less reliably than Claude. Use numbered steps, exact commands, explicit output templates, and state the output language.

## 6. Commands
- **Locations:** `.opencode/commands/<name>.md` and `~/.config/opencode/commands/`. Nested paths become command names with `/` separators.
- **Frontmatter:** `description`, `agent`, `model` (`provider/model#variant`), `subagent` (run in a background child). `subtask` is a deprecated alias for `subagent`.
- **Body placeholders:** `$ARGUMENTS`, `$1`…, `` !`cmd` ``. Stored templates no longer expand `@path`.
- **Prefer skills**, because they work on every platform. `metadata.opencode/slash: "true"` exposes a skill as `/name` in the TUI. Use a command only for a thin launcher, such as one that runs a skill with a fixed agent and model.

## 7. Testing
- **Headless run:**
  ```
  opencode run "<prompt>" --format json [--agent <name>] [--model deepseek/deepseek-flash]
  ```
  Run it from the target directory; there is no `--dir` flag. Use `--worktree <name>` to run in a fresh git worktree. `--format json` prints raw JSON events. Look for `skill` tool calls (trigger tests) and `subagent` calls (delegation).
- **Agents:** list loaded agents in the TUI; there is no `opencode agent list`.
- **Evals:** there is no official runner. Use the stablehand eval protocol with `opencode run`. A `scenario-runner` subagent works for behavior runs.

## 8. Gotchas
- OpenCode also reads `.claude/skills/` and `.agents/skills/`. A same-named variant for another platform overrides or collides by ID (later source wins). Use `.opencode/skills/` and set `OPENCODE_DISABLE_CLAUDE_CODE_SKILLS=1` (see `coexistence.md`).
- Claude tool names (`Read`, `Grep`, `Agent`, …) mean nothing here. Express capabilities through `permissions` actions, and in prose say "read the file", "run the command".
- V1 agent fields (`tools:`, `permission`, `temperature`, `maxSteps`, `name`, …) are deprecated; use `permissions` and the V2 field names. A file that uses any of `permissions`, `system`, `request` or `disabled` is read as V2 and its V1 fields are ignored.
- `opencode run --agent <name>` selects the session agent; a `mode: subagent` agent runs only in a child session, so delegate to it with `@name` or the `subagent` tool, or copy it as `mode: primary` for the test.
- On Windows, the `opencode.ps1` and `pnpm.ps1` shims are blocked by the default PowerShell execution policy; `opencode.cmd` and `pnpm.cmd` work.
- Subagents silently inherit the invoking primary's model. Set `model` explicitly when a subagent needs a different tier.
- `external_directory` is allowed by default in V2. Add an `external_directory` `ask` or `deny` rule to restore a prompt or block outside access.

## 9. Hooks (plugins)

There is no `hooks` key in `opencode.json(c)`. Hooks are **plugins**: packages that export a server part using the `@opencode/plugin` SDK.
- **Locations:** `.opencode/plugins/` (project) and `~/.config/opencode/plugins/` (global) are loaded automatically. Published packages and other directories are listed in the `plugins` array of `opencode.json(c)`.
- **Shape:** the plugin exports `Plugin.define({ id, async setup(ctx) { … } })`; `setup` receives a server client `ctx` and registers tools, hooks, integrations, commands and agents.
- **Source:** opencode.ai/docs/build/plugins and /docs/plugins (checked 2026-11-22). The V1 plugin API (`export const X = async () => ({ "tool.execute.before": … })`) does not run in V2.

Example plugin that registers a server part:
```ts
import { Plugin } from "@opencode/plugin"

export default Plugin.define({
  id: "env-protection",
  async setup(ctx) {
    // register hooks, tools, commands or agents via ctx
  },
})
```
